articles.headline: Prosecutors identify 18 alleged rigged pitches for Clase trial
articles.description: Prosecutors identified 18 pitches, including one from a 2024 playoff game, that will be the focus of their case against Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase that is set for trial in November, according to court documents.
articles.body:
Federal prosecutors have identified 18 pitches, including one from a 2024 playoff game, that will be the focus of their gambling case against Cleveland Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase, which is set for trial in November, according to court documents filed Friday.

In the documents, prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York included a list of the individual pitches that Clase threw in 17 games spanning from May 19, 2023, to May 28, 2025. Clase is accused of sharing advance information about the pitches with bettors, who allegedly placed wagers on the result and velocity of the pitches.

Clase's first pitch to Matt Vierling of the Detroit Tigers in the ninth inning of an Oct. 5, 2024, American League Division Series game was on the list. The pitch, a 93 mph slider, was out of the strike zone. The Guardians won the game 7-0.

Prosecutors allege that Guardians starter Luis Ortiz also participated in the scheme by giving bettors advance information about two of his pitches but did not identify them in the filings.

Clase, Ortiz and two other defendants face wire fraud, money laundering and conspiracy charges. They have pleaded not guilty. Jury selection for the trial is set to begin in November.

In February, the government provided Clase and Ortiz's attorneys with a preliminary list of pitches it was investigating. Ortiz's attorney wrote in a filing at the time that prosecutors had accused Clase of throwing suspect pitches in at least 48 games.

Prosecutors are now focused on 18 pitches from 17 games ahead of the trial, according to the documents.

"The government will only seek to prove that for one or more of approximately 18 of Clase's pitches, and for two of Ortiz's pitches, the defendants provided advance inside information about their pitches to others, who bet on them," U.S. attorney Joseph Nocella wrote.

Clase and Ortiz have been on leave since the summer of 2025. Sportsbooks flagged unusual betting interest on specific pitches from Ortiz in two games in June 2025.

articles.headline: Coventry claim first Premier League win of season at Nottingham Forest
articles.description: Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.
articles.body:
Jay DaSilva fired Coventry to their first Premier League win in 25 years as they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in another game mired by VAR controversy.

Frank Lampard's side have endured a tough return to the top flight, with four defeats and no goals, but they put that right at the fifth attempt at the City Ground on a memorable night.

DaSilva's second-half strike ended their drought and proved enough for a first three points in the top division since the Sky Blues beat Sunderland back in April 2001.

Forest thought they had found a late leveller when Igor Jesus slotted home, but referee Jared Gillett was sent to the monitor by VAR and ruled there was a foul on Caleb Yirenkyi, despite his original on-field decision being a goal.

It left Forest with a burning sense of injustice but, in truth, they did not do enough to take anything from the game.

They are having trouble at the City Ground, having won there just once in the league in front of their own fans since December last year.

The VAR decision means Oliver Glasner's men have yet to score in their first three home games, and it is undermining promising away form where they have taken four points from trips to Liverpool and Aston Villa.

After winning at Villa Park last week, Forest were full of confidence and were straight on the attack, with James McAtee shooting straight at Carl Rushworth from distance after just 50 seconds.

McAtee had another goalbound shot blocked as the Forest attacks kept on coming, with Dan Ndoye unable to finish a nice move by curling just over from 18 yards in the 18th minute.

Liam Delap also had an effort from distance that hit the side-netting as Forest probed without creating anything.

Glasner's men were on the front foot again early in the second half as McAtee had a third effort of the day.

Ndoye and Delap combined down the left, with the striker teeing up the former Manchester City midfielder, but his shot was superbly blocked by Ethan Pinnock.

That proved pivotal as Coventry got a foothold in the game, with Loum Tchaouna shooting straight at Matz Sels.

But Coventry's patient fans finally got their moment 10 minutes into the second half as DaSilva broke their duck.

He raced on to Carl Rushworth's long kick, beat Daniel Munoz, and then fired home in front of the jubilant supporters.

Forest had little in the way of an immediate response as frustrations began to grow.

They began to up the ante in the final 15 minutes and almost levelled when substitute Jesus was denied

by Bobby Thomas' acrobatic clearance off the line.

They had the ball in the back of the net in the 86th minute as Jesus took advantage of a slip by Yirenkyi to roll home.

But for the second home match in a row VAR got involved, with Gillett changing his decision after viewing the monitor and ruling Jesus had clipped the Coventry defender's ankle.

articles.headline: Arsenal 'in trouble from first throw-in' at Brighton - Mikel Arteta
articles.description: Mikel Arteta said he knew Arsenal would be "in trouble" from "the first throw-in" in a 3-0 defeat at Brighton.
articles.headlineJa: ブライトン戦のアーセナルは「最初のスローインから苦しんでいた」― ミケル・アルテタ
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタ監督は、ブライトンに0-3で敗れた試合で「最初のスローインから」アーセナルが苦戦すると分かっていたと明かした。
articles.body:
BRIGHTON, England -- Mikel Arteta said he knew Arsenal would be "in trouble" from "the first throw-in" in a 3-0 defeat at Brighton that ended the champions' unbeaten start to the defence of their Premier League title.

Goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés sealed a convincing and deserved victory for the home side, who climbed to third in the table on the back of the win.

It was the first time Arsenal had lost by three goals in the Premier League since Brighton defeated the Gunners 3-0 at the Emirates in May 2023 and Fabian Hurzeler's side were dominant throughout the game.

But after seeing his side drop points for the first time this season, Arteta said Arsenal had no excuses at the Amex.

"I'm extremely disappointed, but first of all, we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory because they deserved it," Arteta said. "They were the better team.

"From our side, there are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League, but we were very far from [winning] the first duel, the second duel and that put us in a difficult place.

"We made lots of errors, we had no principles of play in situations and we were always on back foot.

"At end of the day, it's a big lesson for us, for all of us."

Brighton coasted to the win despite having 24 hours less recovery time following the midweek Carabao Cup programme. Hurzeler's side won 3-2 at Manchester United on Wednesday while a much-changed Arsenal side beat Ipswich 4-2 at Portman Road on Tuesday.

But despite the advantages in his team's favour, Arteta said that Brighton showed more "bite" and he knew his side would have a bad day "from the first throw-in."

"They [Brighton] knew, we knew, how tough it would be today," Arteta said. "But Brighton overcame us and had another edge that we didn't have.

"Brighton had another bite, their timing was better and when the ball was 50-50, most of the time it was for them.

- Brighton vs. Arsenal player ratings as Gunners slump to hefty defeat against Seagulls

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal's Madueke eyed by Premier League rivals

"From the first throw-in, it was clear that we would be in trouble. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game.

"Credit to Brighton. It doesn't take away from what the team has done the last few weeks.

"But now we have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can happen again."

articles.headline: Steelers rule out WR Pittman Jr. vs. Patriots with foot injury
articles.description: The Steelers will be without another starter for their Week 2 game against the Patriots after downgrading wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to out with a foot injury.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズ、足の負傷でペイトリオッツ戦のWRピットマンJr.を欠場判定
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズは、ワイドレシーバーのマイケル・ピットマンJr.が足の負傷により欠場へ変更されたため、ペイトリオッツとの第2週の試合でまた1人先発選手を欠くことになった。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Ma. -- The Pittsburgh Steelers will be without another starter for their Week 2 game against the New England Patriots after downgrading wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to out with a foot injury.

The Steelers previously ruled cornerback Joey Porter Jr. out after he left Thursday's practice with a back injury during his ramp-up period.

Pittman, who was traded to the Steelers from the Indianapolis Colts in the offseason, popped up on the practice report Wednesday as limited with the foot injury, and he didn't practice Thursday or Friday. Pittman also missed a sizable portion of training camp with an undisclosed injury he appeared to sustain during the team's Saturday night lights practice at Latrobe Memorial Stadium on Aug. 8.

Pittman caught all three targets for 58 yards in the season opener against the Atlanta Falcons, and his presence helped free up top Steelers receiver DK Metcalf.

With Pittman sidelined, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard is likely to see an increase in his workload. The second-round pick and Alabama product played only three snaps in Week 1, but quarterback Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers coaches praised the young pass catcher for his growth throughout the preseason.

"I think he's done a nice job," Rodgers said of Bernard on Sept 2. "He's got a great attitude. He really wants to learn. The best thing I can say about him is he hasn't made repeat mistakes. There's no mistakes going to happen. It's part of the game, especially for young guys. But when he does make a mistake, he takes it to heart and studies it and makes sure he doesn't repeat that thing."

articles.headline: Source: Jets rookie WR Cooper Jr. put on IR with sprained ankle
articles.description: Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., one of the team's three first-round picks, has been placed on injured reserve with a sprained ankle, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ジェッツのルーキーWRクーパーJr.が足首捻挫でIR入り
articles.descriptionJa: チームの1巡目指名選手3人のうちの1人であるジェッツのルーキーWRオマール・クーパーJr.が、足首の捻挫で故障者リスト（IR）に入ったと関係者がNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポート氏に語った。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., one of the team's three first-round picks, was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a sprained ankle, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Cooper, who played only four snaps in the Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans, is expected to return after his four-week IR stint. He is eligible to play Oct. 18 against the New England Patriots.

The Jets now have two wide receivers on injured reserve -- Cooper and Tim Patrick -- leaving them with only four receivers on the active roster for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium.

Chances are the Jets (1-0) will lean heavily on their tight ends in the game plan. They have five on the roster and actually used all five on one play in the 23-10 win over the Titans.

Cooper, drafted 30th overall out of Indiana, made a quick impact in his debut. On the opening possession, he caught a short pass, broke several tackles and turned it into a 30-yard play, setting up a touchdown. After that, he left the game.

He didn't practice all week and was ruled out Friday.

Beyond starters Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, the Jets have Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith at wide receiver. Williams and Smith were targeted only once apiece last week, with Smith dropping his only chance.

For depth purposes, the Jets signed veterans Sterling Shepard and Tyler Johnson this week to the practice squad, but neither is expected to be elevated for Sunday's game.

articles.headline: Arsenal's aura of champions evaporates after Brighton thrash them 3-0
articles.description: The strengths that won Arsenal the title deserted them at Brighton, which celebrated their 125th anniversary with a thumping victory over the champions.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナル、ブライトンに0-3で大敗し王者のオーラが消失
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルにタイトルをもたらした強みがブライトン戦で消え去り、クラブ創立125周年を迎えたブライトンは王者相手に大勝を飾った。
articles.body:
BRIGHTON & HOVE, England -- "Champions of England? You're having a laugh!" As withering chants go, the Brighton & Hove Albion fans' taunting of Arsenal was as brutal as it gets. They even compared them to Tottenham Hotspur.

But more worrying for the Gunners after their 3-0 mauling was that it was caused by two of their most formidable pillars crumbling in this Premier League clash at the Amex Stadium.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: From an A+ to F

- Ranking the hottest men's teams right now: Can anyone stop Barcelona?

- Soccer should learn from the NFL to fix the mess that VAR has created

When Mikel Arteta's team won the title last season, ending the club's 22-year wait to return to the summit of English football in the process, it was an achievement built on solid foundations. They had the best goalkeeper in the country in David Raya, a resolute defense in front of him and the best midfielder in Declan Rice. Arsenal also led the way in scoring from, and defending, set pieces.

But against Fabian Hürzeler's perennially underestimated Brighton, that all deserted them. Rice became the midfielder who was everywhere and nowhere at the same time, while that peerless set piece dominance was exposed when Chema Andrés scored a simple header from a 55th-minute corner and Pascal Struijk headed wide moments later when he should have made it 4-0.

The word "shambles" and Arsenal have not been used together for a long time now. Arteta has seen to that by transforming the team into one of the best in the world. But they were a shambles against Brighton.

Maybe this will prove to be nothing more than a blip, a useful reminder that retaining a title is much harder than winning it in the first place. But Brighton showed that Arsenal's biggest strengths can also be weaknesses if they are tested properly, so how they react to this setback will be a significant test for Arteta and his players.

Arteta now has a three-week international break during which to ponder what went wrong at the Amex before Arsenal's next game, at home to Leeds United on Oct. 10. His biggest concern will be how to get the best out of Rice.

Tightening up at the back and rediscovering their ability to deal with corners should be straightforward enough, as that simply needs a training reset. But if Rice continues to perform as he did at the Amex, Arsenal will have a problem. He played without any kind of tactical or positional discipline, enabling Brighton to dominate the midfield.

Rice can never be questioned for his effort or commitment. He works harder than anyone else on the pitch, but he needs to remember that the best players work smart as well as work hard.

Too often, the England midfielder was chasing back or bursting forward, running out to the right or taking the ball from Raya at the back. As a consequence, he left the midfield empty.
